stats.fact: ComfyUI uses only 4.5GB VRAM for SDXL generation compared to Automatic1111's 7.5GB — 40% more VRAM efficient
Automatic1111 is 10-20% slower than ComfyUI on identical hardware for SDXL generation, with the gap growing for complex workflows
The ComfyUI community created over 1,000 custom node packages in 2026, extending functionality to video generation, advanced editing, and batch processing
ComfyUI's learning curve is real — expect 10-20 hours before feeling comfortable, with basics taking 2-4 hours
In 2026, ComfyUI is the de-facto standard for serious FLUX.2, Stable Diffusion 3.5, HiDream-I1, and video model work
12GB VRAM is the practical minimum for a good all-round ComfyUI experience in 2026; 8GB works for SDXL but feels limiting with FLUX
Flux.1-dev (full fp16/bf16) requires 16-24GB VRAM; 12GB is tight even with optimizations
ComfyUI only recomputes nodes downstream of changes, enabling faster iteration — e.g., tweaking the sampler without re-encoding the prompt

angles: The production pipeline angle: ComfyUI isn't just a UI — it's a reproducible workflow engine where every PNG file IS the workflow, enabling teams to share exact generation parameters
The VRAM efficiency angle: ComfyUI's lazy-evaluation model means you only process what changed, making it dramatically more efficient than A1111 for iterative work
The FLUX migration angle: FLUX.2 cannot run on Automatic1111 at all — developers who want state-of-the-art text-to-image must use ComfyUI
The automation and API angle: ComfyUI exposes a REST/WebSocket API, enabling developers to integrate AI image generation directly into apps and pipelines
The custom node ecosystem angle: 1,000+ community nodes turn ComfyUI into a platform — ControlNet, video generation, face swap, upscaling, and batch processing are all first-class
The debugging-friendly angle: intermediate Preview Image nodes let you inspect results at any step in the pipeline, making complex workflows debuggable
The beginner trap angle: most tutorials start too complex — master the 5 essential nodes first before adding custom nodes
